narration: One in ten Americans is renting a storage unit right now. It feels like a smart temporary fix — but most people keep paying for four years or more, and the math is brutal.
visual: Storage unit door with padlock and horizontal metal slats. '$190/mo' badge springs in. '1 in 10 Americans' stat fades in below.

narration: The average unit runs $190 a month — that's $2,280 a year. And most people signed up thinking 'just a few months.' Sound familiar?
visual: Dollar counter animating up to $2,280 on a dark card. Below it, a 12-month calendar grid fills in square by square as months tick by.

narration: Here's where it gets wild. The typical renter keeps their unit for four years. That's $9,120 total. And sixty-five percent say the stuff inside is worth less than what they've already paid.
visual: Two side-by-side bar charts growing: 'Paid In' bar ($9,120 in red, tall) and 'Stuff Worth' bar (~$1,500 in green, short). Stat quote appears below.

narration: Americans spent thirty-nine point five billion dollars on self-storage last year — more than the entire US film industry. That's not a clutter problem, that's a psychology problem.
visual: A film camera icon labeled 'Hollywood $33B' vs a storage unit icon labeled 'Self-Storage $39.5B'. 'Grew 700% Since 1984' stat appears below.

narration: The real trap is the sunk cost. You've already paid three grand, so quitting feels like admitting you wasted it. But every month you keep paying is a fresh choice to waste even more.
visual: Piggy bank draining with dollar bills flying out toward a storage unit. 'Sunk Cost Trap' badge springs in. Quote: 'I already paid $3,000 so I can't stop now'.

narration: The move that pays: sell or donate everything this weekend. What you truly can't part with probably fits in your home. Bank the rest — follow for more money moves that actually work.
visual: Storage unit door animating open to reveal light inside. Two action buttons appear: 'Sell It' in green and 'Donate' in blue. CTA text springs in at bottom.
